problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{t}^{2}}{2},\,3t+7⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=4.$

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2}+9⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=e.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+9)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+t,4t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=e,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(e) & =⟨2e\operatorname{ln}⁡e+e,4e⟩ \\  & =⟨3e,4e⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=e$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(e),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(e)| & =\sqrt{(3e)^{2}+(4e)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25{e}^{2}} \\  & =5e.\end{aligned}
$$
